lawyer.definition: A professional person authorized to practice law.

attorney.definition: A professional person authorized to practice law.

judge.definition: A public official authorized to decide questions brought before a court of justice.

paralegal.definition: A person with specialized training who assists lawyers.

legal-secretary.definition: An administrative professional who supports lawyers with documents, scheduling, correspondence, and office procedures.
legal-secretary.exampleUsage: The legal secretary organized the case files.

notary.definition: Someone legally empowered to witness signatures and certify a document's validity and to take depositions.

mediator.definition: A negotiator who acts as a link between parties.

arbitrator.definition: Someone chosen to judge and decide a disputed issue.

public-defender.definition: A government-paid lawyer represents people in criminal court when they cannot afford to hire private counsel.

prosecutor.definition: A government official who conducts criminal prosecutions on behalf of the state.

reception.definition: The manner in which something is greeted.

conference-room.definition: A room in a school or office set aside for organized meetings and formal discussion.

law-library.definition: A library containing legal books, court decisions, statutes, and other resources used for legal research.
law-library.exampleUsage: The lawyer checked a reference in the law library.

partner-office.definition: An office assigned to a partner, a senior lawyer who has an ownership or leadership role in a law firm.
partner-office.exampleUsage: The meeting was held in the partner's office.

associate-office.definition: An office assigned to an associate lawyer who works at a law firm without being a partner.
associate-office.exampleUsage: The associate prepared the memo in the associate office.

filing-room.definition: A room used to organize and store paper files and records.
filing-room.exampleUsage: Closed case files were moved to the filing room.

war-room.definition: A dedicated room where leaders coordinate strategy for a military operation or political campaign.

deposition-room.definition: A room used for a formal out-of-court session in which sworn testimony is recorded as part of legal proceedings.
deposition-room.exampleUsage: The attorneys met in the deposition room for recorded testimony.

waiting-area.definition: A room in a place such as an airport or hotel where people sit until they are ready to leave or be served.

records-room.definition: A secure room used to store and manage official records or files.
records-room.exampleUsage: Archived documents were kept in the records room.

criminal-law.definition: The area of law that identifies criminal acts and sets the penalties for them.

civil-law.definition: This area of law resolves noncriminal conflicts involving people, businesses, agreements, possessions, and family relationships.

family-law.definition: This area of law sets rules for marriage, separation, care of children, and bringing children into new families. It also covers other legal matters between family members within a particular place.

corporate-law.definition: The area of law dealing with companies, their formation, governance, transactions, and legal responsibilities.
corporate-law.exampleUsage: The firm has a team that works in corporate law.

tax-law.definition: The systematic study of tax rules, their policy consequences, economic effects, and differences across countries.

immigration-law.definition: The area of law dealing with entry, residence, citizenship, and immigration status under a country's legal system.
immigration-law.exampleUsage: The attorney specializes in immigration law.

real-estate-law.definition: The area of law dealing with land, property ownership, leases, transfers, and related transactions.
real-estate-law.exampleUsage: The firm handles contracts involving real-estate law.

employment-law.definition: The area of law governing relationships between employers and workers, including workplace rights and obligations.
employment-law.exampleUsage: The seminar covered basic principles of employment law.

environmental-law.definition: The system of laws that safeguards nature by limiting pollution and managing the use of land, water, and other resources.

intellectual-property.definition: Legal protections give creators control over the use of their original works and inventions.

consult.definition: To get or ask advice from.

represent.definition: To be a delegate or spokesperson for.

file.definition: A named collection of digital information saved on a device.

appeal.definition: (law) a legal proceeding in which the appellant resorts to a higher court for the purpose of obtaining a review of a lower court decision and a reversal of the lower court's judgment or the granting of a new trial.

negotiate.definition: To discuss the terms of an arrangement.

draft.definition: An early version of writing that can still be changed.

review.definition: An article that evaluates a book, film, product, or event.
